_method_summary: The morphospace findings as a render-from-data feed. Prose is authored interpretation; every NUMBER is pulled live from the 4 source feeds and injected — nothing hardcoded. Re-run after refining the morphospace and the findings update.
title: What the morphospace is teaching us
subtitle: Findings from the instrument — not how we build, but what we are learning about meaning-making.
status: v1 · numbers computed on the current (pre-rebalance) coords; regenerate after the Islamic+Jewish atlas batch lands

headline.claim: Traditions converge without being the same, and differ without being incommensurable — and you can measure which is which, axis by axis.
headline.gloss: Positionality-as-coordinates says the thing the universal-vs-particular binary structurally cannot: a text can be tradition-specific on one axis and convergent on another, at the same time. The convergence is a measured, located fact — not a claim.

cuts.name: The map (archetypes)
cuts.method: speMCA-style MCA (not-engaged + rare values set PASSIVE, not dropped)
cuts.question: Do recurring positions cut across traditions?
cuts.result: 4 archetypes, each spanning 6–16 traditions across 3173 coded reads: Devotional-Covenantal (n=1007, 8 traditions), Prophetic (n=894, 6 traditions), Critical-Deconstructive (n=554, 16 traditions), Emergent-Relational (n=718, 16 traditions).
cuts.reading: Every archetype is occupied by many traditions in their own voices — rhyme, not identity.

cuts.name: Interleaving
cuts.method: cross-tradition nearest-neighbor rate (k=10), computed at the TRADITION tier
cuts.question: Do traditions cluster in their own corners, or interleave? (axis-free)
cuts.result: MACRO 86% (equal-tradition weight, 14 traditions). Christianity 8% (n=2262) is the ONLY tradition that looks clustered; every other tradition mixes 76–99%.
cuts.reading: The low rate tracks CLASS SIZE, not distinctiveness: Christianity is ~92% of the Abrahamic reads, so its neighbors are Christian by default. Un-lumping 'Abrahamic' (family MACRO was 79%) makes the prevalence mechanism visible.

cuts.name: Prevalence curve
cuts.question: Is the apparent separation real, or a corpus-skew artifact?
cuts.result: Raw silhouette +0.24 → -0.05 when classes are balanced.
cuts.reading: Silhouette runs -1..+1: +1 = tight separate clusters, 0 = interleaved, negative = closer to OTHER groups than your own. The raw +0.24 looks like separation; balance the classes and it collapses to -0.05. The 'separation' was manufactured by a corpus that is ~78% Christianity. The collapse IS the finding.

surprises.title: Texts differ most in HOW MUCH they engage, not in what they claim.
surprises.finding: The dominant raw axis (dim1, 28% inertia) was engagement-breadth — how many of the eight questions a text even touches — not 'observed vs revealed'. The first thing that separates texts is whether they speak on a dimension at all. That is honest, not broken: it is why the method separates an engagement layer from a content layer.

surprises.title: Abrahamic isn't special — it's just big.
surprises.finding: Its 8% cross-tradition rate reads as a tight cluster, but it is pure prevalence (~92% of it is Christianity). Freed from the lump, Islam mixes 91% and Judaism 90%, like every other tradition.

surprises.title: Diversity doesn't just add data — it reveals dimensions.
surprises.finding: Adding African, Pacific, Aboriginal, and Native traditions (kinship/ancestral/belonging-heavy) grew a whole new third axis (unitive↔relational, dim3 18% — nearly dim2's 19%) that the mostly-Abrahamic early sample literally could not see.

surprises.title: Your own data lied at first glance.
surprises.finding: Naïvely the numbers say traditions DIVERGE (silhouette +0.24) — the opposite of the truth. Skew doesn't just hide structure, it manufactures false structure. Corrected (balanced), the signal is convergence (-0.05).

surprises.title: Convergence is rhyme, not identity.
surprises.finding: A Buddhist Sanctuary text is still Buddhist; it just shares a coordinate with a Christian one. The archetypes aren't the universal truth behind religions — they are recurring positions traditions independently occupy, each in its own voice. That is little-t/Big-T made geometric: little-t = the shared coordinate, Big-T = the voice.

argument_universal_vs_particular.title: Why positionality-as-a-space (vs collapsing to universal-vs-particular)
points: The binary forces a false choice: collapse toward the universal and you erase the particular (perennialism — usually the majority's view in disguise); insist on the particular and you lose comparison (mute relativism). Neither holds resemblance AND distinctness at once.
The space refuses the choice: a text isn't universal OR particular — it has coordinates. It can be tradition-specific on ontology and convergent on telos, located dimension by dimension.
Convergence stops being a claim and becomes a measured, located fact: not 'everything is one' but 'this move appears in Buddhism and Christianity and Yoruba — each in its own vocabulary'.
'Universal' was never a place you could stand: there is no view-from-nowhere. In the morphospace there is no outside — 'universal' is just a region where many positions happen to land.
Tonight is the proof the coarse binary would have lied: ask 'same or different?' on the raw data → 'different' → wrong (a skew artifact). The binary can't self-correct; the space can.

method_foundation.note: What methods we reuse here and why (the drawer's foundation).

glossary.what: PCA's cousin for categorical data — turns 'which value on each of 8 axes' into x/y/z.
glossary.why: what we've used; its math inflates rare + sentinel categories, which is why dim1 became engagement-breadth.

glossary.what: MCA where chosen categories are marked PASSIVE (projected, not driving the axes).
glossary.why: the fix for the extremes: (not-engaged) + rare values passive → the clean archetype biplot. Passive ≠ dropped.

glossary.what: Gower = a '% of axes on which two texts differ' distance handling missing/rare gracefully; PCoA turns it into coordinates.
glossary.why: the IRR234 cohort's pick for the PRIMARY clustering question — less sensitive to rare-value inflation than MCA (post-Saquib refactor).

glossary.what: 'how many hidden profiles best explain the data?'
glossary.why: downgraded by the diverse cohort — answers 'how many types', not 'do texts cluster by tradition'. Optional benchmark only.

method_foundation.decision: Saquib demo: MCA / speMCA-approx (built + reproducible now). Locked refactor (post-Saquib, IRR234): Gower+PCoA primary + speMCA for the interpretable biplot; LCA at most a benchmark. We've DECIDED the refactor, not yet done it — that honesty belongs on the page.

validity.question: Are the tradition labels defined independently of the 8 coding axes, or partly inferred from them (circularity)?
validity.answer: Independent. tradition_id is stamped on the SOURCE at ingestion (provenance — 'this is a Qur'an'), across 550 traditions, NOT inferred from the coded axes. So the clustering test uses an external grouping variable — it is not circular. (DeepSeek's cross-check, answered.)

validity.question: What level do we compute traditions at — family, tradition, or sub-tradition?
validity.answer: Locked at the TRADITION tier (2-segment: Christianity / Islam / Buddhism / Daoism …). Family (Abrahamic) lumps three world religions and hides the prevalence mechanism; sub-tradition (Lutheran) is too sparse (n<10). The tradition tier is the honest, consistent middle.

validity.question: Is the 3rd axis inside the 2×2 archetypes, or a separate dimension?
validity.answer: A separate, orthogonal 3rd dimension (unitive↔relational), not inside the 2×2. It carries 18% inertia vs dim2's 19% — nearly equal — so it's shown BESIDE the archetypes (a dim1×dim3 panel), never folded into them.

how_to_extend: Append a finding-object to cuts / surprises / validity and re-run this builder. Numbers are pulled live from the 4 source feeds — never type a figure into the prose. Method / Design / Library have append-access; the page is a growing ledger.
